questions.stem: How does Data Harmonisation go one step beyond Data Integration, Data Blending, Data Warehousing and Data Marts?
options: It only connects to a single source system
It standardises data from multiple source systems into one unified format, becoming a bridge between data and business requirements
It stores data without any transformation
It removes the need for business stakeholders
It replaces ETL with manual data entry
questions.explanation: All of these bring data from disparate sources into one place, but Data Harmonisation goes further by standardising it into one unified format that bridges data and business requirements.

questions.stem: What does 'one unified format' mean in the context of Data Harmonisation?
options: All data is stored as text
All data is stored in a single table
All data is converted to a single currency
Data is converted in such a way that it becomes accurate for someone
All data is stored in a spreadsheet
questions.explanation: One unified format means data is converted in such a way that it can become accurate for someone, that is, fit for a specific purpose.

questions.stem: Harmonising data in one location for a specific department can be called what?
options: A Data Mart
A Data Lake
A Data Mashup
A Data Swamp
A Data Mesh
questions.explanation: Harmonising data in one location for a specific department can be called a Data Mart.

questions.stem: Defining standard naming conventions, data types and codes from multiple sources in one unique format is described as harmonising data for what?
options: Data Lineage
Data Visualisation
Master Data Management
Data Monetisation
Data Splitting
questions.explanation: Defining standard naming conventions, data types and codes from multiple sources in one unique format is harmonising data for Master Data Management.

questions.stem: Gathering metadata details of all source systems, data lakes, warehouses and marts up to reports and dashboards is harmonising data for what?
options: Data Marts
Master Data Management
Data Enrichment
Data Ethics
Data Lineage
questions.explanation: Gathering metadata across all systems from sources through to reports and dashboards is harmonising data for Data Lineage.

questions.stem: Why is the involvement of business stakeholders described as a must-have step in Data Harmonisation?
options: Because they approve the IT budget
Because they write the ETL code
Because without functional knowledge, garbage will flow in
Because they own the database licences
Because they define the latitude and longitude values
questions.explanation: Business stakeholders must be involved because without functional knowledge garbage will flow into the harmonised data.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the ideal steps for conducting Data Harmonisation?
options: Understand the vision of the business requirements, that is, what the converted data will be used for
Set the baseline by identifying all relevant source systems, tables and columns
Define standard processes and actions such as ETL, ELT or manual steps
Skip reconciliation once the initial load is complete
Define metadata at each step of the harmonisation process
questions.explanation: Regular reconciliation and monitoring are a key step so that data quality is not compromised; skipping them is the opposite of the guidance.

questions.stem: Which department is used as the example of one that can perform poorly without harmonised data, and what does it depend on?
options: The Marketing department, which depends on product names, codes, sales locations, timing and buyer details to plan campaigns
The Legal department, which depends on contract templates
The HR department, which depends on leave balances
The IT department, which depends on server logs
The Facilities department, which depends on printer ink orders
questions.explanation: The Marketing department heavily depends on product names, codes, sales locations, dates, times, buyer demographics, events and holidays to plan accurate campaigns, messages and events.

questions.stem: Would the details harmonised for the Marketing department be equally relevant to the Finance department?
options: Yes, every department needs exactly the same harmonised details
No, for the Finance department the harmonisation steps and required details will be totally different
Yes, because Finance owns the marketing budget
No, because Finance does not use data
Yes, because harmonisation always produces one universal dataset
questions.explanation: The details highlighted for Marketing might not be relevant to Finance; for the Finance department the Data Harmonisation steps and required details will be totally different.

questions.stem: What is the first ideal step in conducting Data Harmonisation?
options: Define the ETL processes
Reconcile the loaded data
Define metadata for every table
Buy a Master Data Management tool
Understand the vision of the business requirements, that is, what purpose the converted data will serve
questions.explanation: The ideal steps begin with understanding the vision of the business requirements, in other words what the converted data will be used for.
